title: Docker from the kernel up
intro: What a container really is underneath docker run: one ordinary Linux process, fenced in by namespaces and held to limits by cgroups, on the same kernel as everything else. Every puzzle shows real output from a real machine, and you can run the same commands yourself. For Android and Kotlin engineers who use Docker but have never looked under it.
how: Each puzzle starts with a problem, gives you one building block, shows it in a diagram that plays itself, and ends with three questions. Every output on the page was produced on a real test machine (Docker Engine 29.9.2 on an Ubuntu 24.04 userland in a Firecracker microVM, custom kernel 6.18.44, cgroup v1) and you can reproduce it under Run it yourself. Facts come from Docker's documentation, the Linux manual pages, the kernel documentation and the Open Container Initiative specifications, quoted on every page.

modules.title: Module 1: What a container really is
modules.blurb: Find a container's program in the host's process list, compare it with a virtual machine, then open the fence one piece at a time: process IDs, files, hostname and network, users and capabilities, memory limits, processor time, and finally who builds it all when you type docker run.

upcoming.title: Module 2: Images
upcoming.topics: Layers as stacked file changes, overlayfs (lower and upper directories, copy-up, whiteouts), overlay2 versus the containerd image store, the writable layer, content-addressed digests versus movable tags, registries (pulling, authentication, mirrors, rate limits), and the OCI image spec: index, manifest, config, layers and referrers.

upcoming.title: Module 3: The Dockerfile and the build
upcoming.topics: Which instructions make layers, the build context and .dockerignore, the build cache's rules, multi-stage builds, BuildKit (cache and secret mounts, remote caches, bake), reproducible builds, and provenance and SBOM attestations.

upcoming.title: Module 4: Running a container well
upcoming.topics: PID 1 and signals, exec form versus shell form, docker stop's grace period and --init, exit codes (128 + signal, OOMKilled), restart policies and health checks, logs and their drivers (json-file needs max-size), and ulimits.

upcoming.title: Module 5: Data and networking
upcoming.topics: Volumes versus bind mounts versus tmpfs, the bridge network and veth pairs, publishing ports through iptables or nftables, user-defined networks and the embedded DNS, host, none and macvlan, IPv6, Compose, and rootless networking.

upcoming.title: Module 6: Limits and failures
upcoming.topics: cgroup v2 first: the OOM kill in depth (memory.events), memory.high, pressure stall information, CPU weight versus quota and throttling, io.max, a JVM in a container, PIDs limits, and disk space and prune.

upcoming.title: Module 7: Security
upcoming.topics: Non-root users, capabilities, --privileged and no-new-privileges, seccomp, AppArmor and SELinux, devices, read-only filesystems, rootless mode and idmapped mounts, secrets in env and inspect, scanning, SBOMs and signing with cosign or Notation, and the Docker socket.

upcoming.title: Module 8: Small, fast images, and Docker in your own work
upcoming.topics: Distroless and Alpine trade-offs (musl versus glibc), layer ordering, multi-architecture images with buildx, an Android Gradle build in a container, Testcontainers for Kotlin tests, Docker in CI, and Docker Desktop for Mac users.

upcoming.title: Module 9: To production
upcoming.topics: Promoting an image by digest, a bridge to Kubernetes pods and CRI, debugging a running container (exec, inspect, nsenter, a debug container), a container that won't start, live restore and daemon upgrades, and rebuilding for security fixes.
